reviewDecisions.rationale: Q2 evolves from possible tariff front-loading into observable EOL-driven DDR4 scarcity and price acceleration; company conversion bridge is testable.
Two independent first-party suppliers confirm a persistent equipment cycle; v0.9 requires direct A-share earnings conversion rather than backlog proxy.
Two independent Reuters observations show policy became a measurable physical magnet shortage; value-chain incidence remains the key research question.
Record/front-loaded project activity coexisted with module-manufacturer losses, creating a useful value-chain mapping problem rather than a generic solar long.
Broad manufacturing weakness is a timing/contradiction input, not a company-selection thesis.
Broad PPI deflation lacks a narrow beneficiary and is better used as margin context.
